EV: Every. Used in aviation scheduling, NOTAMs, and operational logs to indicate each occurrence or instance.
EVS: Enhanced vision system (EVS). An aircraft-mounted sensor system (typically infrared or millimeter-wave radar) that projects an enhanced image of the external scene onto a head-up display (HUD), enabling pilots to see runways and terrain in low-visibility conditions.
EXC: Except. Used in NOTAMs and ATC instructions to indicate an exclusion or exception to a rule or restriction.
FAC: Facility. A general aviation term for any physical installation, such as an airport, navigation aid, ATC unit, or maintenance base.
FAP: Final approach point (FAP). The point in an instrument approach procedure (typically for non-precision approaches) where the final approach segment begins; equivalent to the final approach fix (FAF) for precision approaches.
FAS: Final approach segment (FAS). The segment of an instrument approach procedure from the final approach fix (FAF) or final approach point (FAP) to the missed approach point (MAPt); the phase of flight where the aircraft is aligned with the runway for landing.
FAX: Facsimile. Used in aviation documentation to refer to facsimile transmission of charts, weather products, or flight documents.
FC: Funnel cloud. An ICAO weather phenomenon code used in METAR to report a funnel cloud or tornado that is not reaching the ground; indicates a rotating column of air extending from a cumuliform cloud.
FCST: Forecast. A prediction of future meteorological conditions, used in aviation weather briefings, flight planning, and TAF (Terminal Aerodrome Forecast) products.
FCT: Friction coefficient. A measure of runway surface condition, typically on a scale from 0 (poor) to 1 (good), used for aircraft landing performance calculations.
FDPS: Flight data processing system. An ATC automation system that processes and distributes flight plan data to controller positions for en-route and terminal air traffic management.
FEW: Few. A METAR/TAF cloud cover descriptor indicating 1 to 2 oktas (one to two-eighths) of sky coverage; used in aviation weather reports to specify the amount of cloud layer.
FG: Fog. An ICAO weather phenomenon code used in METAR/TAF to report fog with visibility less than 1000 meters (5/8 statute mile); a significant hazard for takeoff, landing, and taxi operations.
FIC: Flight information centre. A facility that provides aeronautical and meteorological information, flight planning assistance, and in-flight advisory services to pilots within a defined area.
FIR: Flight information region. A defined volume of airspace within which flight information service and alerting service are provided; the basic unit of airspace delegation under ICAO.
FIS: Flight information service. A service provided by ATC or flight information centres to supply pilots with essential meteorological and operational information for safe flight.
FLD: Field. Used in NOTAMs and aviation reports to refer to an airfield, airport, or any defined area used for aircraft operations.
FLG: Flashing. Used to describe lights or signals that operate with intermittent illumination, such as strobe lights, beacon lights, or visual approach slope indicators.
FLR: Flare. A pyrotechnic device carried on aircraft for emergency signaling; also refers to the visual signal produced by such a device.
FLT: Flight. A generic term used in ATC communications, flight plans, and operational logs to refer to any aircraft journey or scheduled air service.
FLTCK: Flight check. A specialized flight operation conducted to evaluate the performance of navigation aids, instrument approach procedures, or ATC equipment in a specific area.
FLW: Follow. ATC instruction to proceed behind or in sequence after another aircraft, vehicle, or specified guidance path.
FLY: Fly. An ATC instruction or clearance to proceed by flight (versus taxiing); also used in phraseology such as 'fly heading' to direct a pilot to steer a specific compass course.
FMC: Flight management computer. The primary onboard computer that automates navigation, performance optimization, and flight planning functions in modern transport aircraft.
FMS: Flight management system. An integrated aircraft system that combines navigation, flight planning, performance management, and guidance functions, typically comprising the FMC and related sensors.
FMU: Flow management unit. An ATC unit responsible for monitoring and managing traffic demand, implementing flow control measures (miles-in-trail, ground stops, etc.) to balance capacity and demand.
FNA: Final approach. The phase of flight from the final approach fix (FAF) to the runway threshold or missed approach point; the final descent and alignment segment of an instrument approach.
FPAP: Flight path alignment point (FPAP). A point used in Localizer Performance with Vertical guidance (LPV) approaches that defines the lateral and vertical alignment of the approach path; part of the SBAS (Satellite-Based Augmentation System) approach design.
FPL: Filed flight plan. A standardized document submitted to ATC before departure specifying the aircraft identification, route, altitude, speed, and other operational details for the planned flight.
FPM: Feet per minute. A unit of vertical speed used in aviation for rate of climb/descent; standard values include 500 fpm (typical approach descent rate) to 3000+ fpm (military climb).
FPR: Flight plan route. The specific path defined by waypoints, airways, and fixes that an aircraft intends to follow from departure to destination, as filed in the flight plan.
FR: Fuel remaining. A fuel status indicator communicated to ATC during emergencies or priority situations to indicate the amount of fuel remaining on board.
FREQ: Frequency. The specific radio frequency assigned for ATC communications, navigation aids, or approach/departure procedures; a critical element of all ATC clearances.
FRNG: Firing. Used in NOTAMs and airspace restrictions to indicate areas where live-fire military exercises or weapons testing is in progress; a hazard for civil aviation.
FRONT: Front. The boundary between two air masses of different temperature and density, often associated with significant weather changes, turbulence, and instrument flight conditions.
FRQ: Frequent. Used in aviation reports and NOTAMs to describe weather phenomena or operational events that occur repeatedly over a short time span.
FSL: Full stop landing. A landing in which the aircraft comes to a complete stop on the runway, as opposed to a touch-and-go or stop-and-go; standard for most commercial operations.
FSS: Flight service station. An FAA facility that provides preflight weather briefings, flight plan filing, in-flight radio communications, and search-and-rescue coordination services to pilots.
FST: First. Used in sequencing and prioritization contexts, such as 'first come, first served' in ATC arrival sequencing or 'first officer' in crew coordination.
FT: Feet. Feet. The standard unit of altitude measurement in aviation for the US and many other countries; used for altitudes, heights, RVR values, and runway lengths.
FTE: Flight technical error (FTE). The difference between the aircraft's actual position and the desired position along the intended flight path; a measure of pilot or autopilot tracking accuracy used in performance-based navigation (PBN) standards.
FTP: Fictitious threshold point (FTP). A defined point in space used in approach procedure design that serves as the runway threshold for navigation purposes, even when the physical threshold is displaced; commonly used in LPV and other GPS-based approaches.
FTT: Flight technical tolerance (FTT). The maximum allowable deviation from the intended flight path for a given navigation specification; used in performance-based navigation (PBN) to define containment limits and required navigation performance (RNP) accuracy.
FU: Smoke. An ICAO weather phenomenon code used in METAR to report smoke in the atmosphere, typically from wildfires or industrial sources, which can reduce visibility and create navigation hazards.
FZ: Freezing. A descriptor used in METAR/TAF codes to indicate freezing conditions, typically followed by a precipitation type (e.g., FZDZ, FZRA, FZFG); signifies sub-freezing temperatures causing ice accretion on aircraft and surfaces.
FZDZ: Freezing drizzle. An ICAO weather code for freezing drizzle; drizzle that falls as liquid but freezes on contact with surfaces at or below freezing temperature, creating hazardous icing conditions on runways and aircraft.
FZFG: Freezing fog. An ICAO weather code for freezing fog; fog in which supercooled water droplets freeze on contact with surfaces, producing rime ice accretion on aircraft, runways, and airport infrastructure.
FZRA: Freezing rain. An ICAO weather code for freezing rain; rain that falls as liquid but freezes upon impact with cold surfaces, creating clear ice accretion on aircraft wings, control surfaces, and runways.
G/A: Ground-to-air. A designation for radio communications transmitted from a ground station to an aircraft; used in ATC communications to specify the direction of transmission.
G/A/G: Ground-to-air and air-to-ground. A designation for two-way radio communications between ground stations and aircraft, covering both transmission directions in air-ground communication systems.
GAIN: Airspeed or headwind gain. In aviation performance calculations, the increase in indicated airspeed or the beneficial effect of a headwind component during takeoff, climb, or approach; also refers to the advantage gained from wind conditions during specific phases of flight.
